title: Sorting position bounded by a value count
statement: Let $k:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ and let $N,j\in\mathbb{N}$ with $j<N$. The position assigned to $j$ when the first $N$ indices are sorted by their $k$-values, breaking ties by increasing index, is strictly less than the number of indices among the first $N$ whose $k$-value is less than $k(j)+1$.
hypotheses_covered: $k$ is a function from natural numbers to natural numbers.
